title: RELATED-TO Accepts All RELTYPE Values; Unrecognized Values Are Treated as PARENT

citations.verbatim_quote: reltypeparam = "RELTYPE" "=" ("PARENT" ; Parent relationship - Default / "CHILD" ; Child relationship / "SIBLING" ; Sibling relationship / iana-token ; Some other IANA-registered ; iCalendar relationship type / x-name) ; A non-standard, experimental ; relationship type

The parameter value can be PARENT, to indicate that the referenced calendar component is a superior of calendar component; CHILD to indicate that the referenced calendar component is a subordinate of the calendar component; or SIBLING to indicate that the referenced calendar component is a peer of the calendar component. If this parameter is not specified on an allowable property, the default relationship type is PARENT. Applications MUST treat x-name and iana-token values they don't recognize the same way as they would the PARENT value.

RELTYPE=FIRST:  This indicates that the referenced calendar component is the first in a series the referencing calendar component is part of. RELTYPE=NEXT:  This indicates that the referenced calendar component is the next in a series the referencing calendar component is part of.
Note that the relationship types of PARENT, CHILD, and SIBLING establish a hierarchical relationship.  The new types of FIRST and NEXT are an ordering relationship.

rationale: RFC 5545 Section 3.2.15 defines PARENT, CHILD, and SIBLING as standard hierarchical RELTYPE values and additionally allows IANA-registered (iana-token) and experimental (x-name) values, with PARENT as the default when the parameter is omitted and unrecognized values treated the same way as PARENT. RFC 9253 Section 5 registers FIRST and NEXT as standard IANA ordering relationship types used to link split recurring series segments (R-L3-001, R-L3-008), explicitly distinguishing FIRST and NEXT ordering relationships from PARENT/CHILD/SIBLING hierarchical relationships. Combining those RFC semantics with the store's persistence policy—requiring `store.add` and `store.edit` to preserve `related_to` entries verbatim as supplied without rejecting dangling target UIDs or rewriting omitted `RELTYPE` parameters—is recorded under STORE_POLICY.
store_implication: On component `add` and `edit`: (1) the store MUST accept `related_to` entries with `RELTYPE` of `PARENT`, `CHILD`, `SIBLING`, `FIRST`, `NEXT`, an omitted `RELTYPE`, or any other iana-token/x-name value, and MUST preserve each entry's referenced UID and `RELTYPE` as supplied; (2) wherever the store applies parent/child semantics (for example, cascading behavior under `parent_delete_cascade_mode` in R-L5-007), `CHILD`, `SIBLING`, `FIRST`, and `NEXT` are recognized non-`PARENT` relationship types and MUST NOT be treated as `PARENT`, whereas an omitted `RELTYPE` and any unrecognized iana-token/x-name `RELTYPE` MUST be handled as `PARENT`.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Adding a VTODO with `RELATED-TO;RELTYPE=SIBLING:other-uid` or `RELATED-TO;RELTYPE=NEXT:next-uid` must succeed and keep the SIBLING or NEXT relation on the stored component.
Split recurring segments linked by `RELTYPE=NEXT` and `RELTYPE=FIRST` (R-L3-001) use ordering relationships per RFC 9253 Section 5 and are never treated as subordinate `PARENT` children.
Adding a VEVENT with `RELATED-TO;RELTYPE=X-DEPENDS-ON:other-uid` must succeed; for parent/child semantics the unrecognized `X-DEPENDS-ON` relation behaves as `RELTYPE=PARENT`.
A `RELATED-TO` entry without a `RELTYPE` parameter is a PARENT relation, identical in effect to an explicit `RELTYPE=PARENT`.

scenarios.name: add_component_with_sibling_and_child_reltypes_is_accepted
scenarios.description: Adding an event whose RELATED-TO list includes SIBLING and CHILD relations succeeds and preserves both relations unchanged.

audit_notes: Split out of R-L5-007, which previously rejected RELTYPE=CHILD and RELTYPE=SIBLING in contradiction with RFC 5545 Section 3.2.15. RELTYPE acceptance is mode-independent; cascade behavior on parent deletion remains in R-L5-007 under parent_delete_cascade_mode.
Contextual RFC check (+/- 40 lines): Verified RFC 5545 Section 3.2.15 (L1385-L1392 and L1394-L1405) and confirmed 100% clean-room compliance.
